cohort: 17,230 healthy pregnant women without medical or obstetric risk factors other than obesity
finding: While obesity was associated with increased risk of some interventions and adverse outcomes, the overall risk for interventions or outcomes requiring obstetric care was modestly increased in otherwise healthy women.
mod_finding: This study found that while obesity was associated with an increased risk of augmentation and intrapartum cesarean section, multiparous obese women may have lower overall intrapartum risks than previously appreciated.
